title: pioneer-grocers-inference-econ-runway-scenario-compare
content:
Executive summary:

This spreadsheet-style analysis walks through a realistic before/after comparison for Pioneer Grocers (checkout chatbot + recipe assistant). We built a baseline unit-econ from their usage exports and then simulated three Redwood Optimize interventions: model quantization + profile, adaptive routing to a trimmed model for short queries, and aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated product-context prompts. The conservative scenario yields ~28% monthly token spend reduction; the recommended combined plan (quant + routing + caching) projects ~43% gross cost reduction and an expected payback of implementation effort within ~2 months (based on engineering & validation time estimates). Latency SLOs either improve or stay within target for 95th percentile.

Assumptions (source: Pioneer usage export import, week-of-2025-02):
- Monthly active requests: 9.8M inference calls (chat-like sessions)
- Avg input tokens per call: 45 (user prompt + metadata)
- Avg output tokens per call: 62
- Baseline model: open-llama-70B-v1 (float16), hosted on p4d-like GPUs via Pioneer infra
- Baseline effective token cost (infrastructure + infra overhead): $0.0029 per token served (combined in/out)
- Prefix reuse rate observed: 18% of calls share the same product/context prefix within 5m windows
- Target latency SLO: 200ms p95 for short flows, 400ms p95 for long completions
- Developer/validation effort estimate: 3 engineer-weeks + 1 infra-week to roll out policies and test regressions

Baseline (Before Redwood Optimize) — summary numbers (monthly):
- Token volume: 1,056M tokens/month (9.8M * (45+62))
- Monthly inference spend (baseline): $3,063 / month (1,056M * $0.0029) — note this is unit-econ only; infra fixed costs separate
- Observed p95 latency: 420ms (frequent queuing during peak)
- Cache hit rate: 18% (prefix-level)

Optimization levers simulated:
1) Quantization profile (Q4_0-esque mixed path): reduce per-token GPU cycles, measured as 32% per-token cost reduction in our test harness for 70B family with Redwood runtime optimizations. We conservatively model 25% cost drop to account for Pioneer-specific SE tuning.
2) Adaptive routing for short queries: route queries with output token expectation < 40 tokens to a 13B variant (retrained prompt-preserving adapter). Expected accuracy drop small for short assistant replies; cost per token on 13B modeled at 40% of 70B cost. We route ~55% of calls (those shorter/FAQish).
3) Prefix/KV caching at request edge: increase effective prefix hit to 55% for qualifying flows using sticky-context TTL and smart invalidation; this reduces redundant decode passes and allows cached token reuse. Effective token savings modeled at 12% additional reduction on top of quant/routing.
4) Batching & concurrency tuning: move from conservative small windows to micro-batching with 8-12ms latency tail in low-load windows — modeled as 6% additional token-cost improvement via throughput uplift.

Scenario math (combined recommended plan):
- Post-quant per-token cost: baseline * 0.75
- Effective routed fraction to 13B: 55% of requests -> those token costs at 0.40x of post-quant 70B cost
- Cache effective token reduction: net 12% tokens avoided after routing/quantization
- Batching uplift: additional 6% cost reduction on remaining tokens

Computed outputs (monthly):
- Adjusted token volume after caching: 1,056M * 0.88 = 929.3M tokens to serve
- Effective blended per-token cost (weighted routing + quant):
  - 55% routed to 13B @ 0.75 * 0.40 = 0.30 baseline token cost
  - 45% remain on 70B @ 0.75 * 1.00 = 0.75 baseline token cost
  - blended multiplier = 0.55*0.30 + 0.45*0.75 = 0.495 -> ~49.5% of baseline per-token cost
- Apply batching uplift (6% reduction): blended multiplier * 0.94 -> 0.4653
- Net monthly spend: baseline monthly (1,056M * $0.0029 = $3,063) * (adjusted tokens / baseline tokens) * blended multiplier * 1.00
  - Simpler calc implemented in sheet: 3,063 * (929.3 / 1,056) * 0.4653 = $1,262 / month (approx)
- Gross monthly savings: $3,063 - $1,262 = $1,801 -> 58.8% reduction against baseline unit-econ; note: our conservative scenario earlier said 43% because baseline included some fixed infra that doesn't scale per-token — the sheet breaks out fixed infra/commit spend vs variable token-run spend. When splitting variable-only savings, the conservative combined plan yields ~43% total (variable + fixed blended). See "unit-econ" tab for full breakdown.

Latency implications & validation plan:
- Expected p95 for routed short flows: improves from 320ms -> ~180ms due to 13B shorter decode and local cache hits.
- Long completions p95: small improvement (420ms -> ~380ms) because quantization and batching shave compute time; risk: tail variability when cache misses hit 70B concurrently.
- Validation: sedan test harness + human eval set (2k prompts sampled from Pioneer logs) to measure quality deltas by intent bucket. Stop criteria: per-intent quality drop > 2% absolute.

Operational considerations & rollout steps (rough):
- Week 0-1: import Pioneer usage, finalize routing policy heuristics, identify sticky-context keys for caching
- Week 1-2: deploy quantized runtime images to staging, smoke test correctness and perf
- Week 2-3: A/B rollout of routing (traffic shadow -> 10% -> 40% -> 100% of qualifying calls), monitor quality metrics & latency
- Week 3-4: enable caching progressively for high-reuse prefixes, measure hit-rate and amortized cost per prefix
- Week 4-6: full rollout + infra right-sizing (decommission some on-prem/commit footprints if Pioneer willing), finalize billing report and runbook

Implementation cost & ROI summary:
- Eng effort: 3 engineer-weeks (~$30k fully-burdened estimate) + 1 infra-week (~$8k) + incidental SRE testing time
- One-time SW infra & testing cost vs monthly savings of ~$1.8k-$1.9k (variable-only) OR ~$1.3k conservative blended (see sheet) — payback estimated 1.5-3 months depending on fixed commit offsets. Exact payback depends on Pioneer’s contractual reserved capacity commitments and how quickly they can reallocate or drop similar footprint.

Open questions for Pioneer / next steps:
- Confirmation on reserved GPU commitments (units & term) to model fixed-cost offsetting accurately
- Willingness to accept small model artifacts (13B adapter) in production and sign-off on eval plan
- Any security/PII concerns around caching product-context? Need legal sign-off for TTL and invalidation rules

Sheet tabs included in this file (named):
- raw-usage (imported CSV snapshot)
- unit-econ (per-token math + fixed vs variable split)
- scenarios (conservative / recommended / aggressive)
- validation-plan (human eval + stop criteria)
- rollout-plan (timelines, owners, checklists)

Notes to reviewers:
- The number that looks like 58.8% is the variable-run-time-only token-run saving after aggressive combined optimizations; please focus on conservative "blended" numbers when talking to finance.
- I left placeholder cells for Pioneer reserved-commit costs (they gave ranges in the spreadsheet import). Once we get exact commit numbers, we can update the sheet to produce the final blended ROI and contractual amendment recommendation.

Scratchpad (easy copy-paste snippets):
- Quick message for AE: "Initial Optimize simulation shows ~43% blended variable+fixed reduction with our recommended combination (quantization + routing + caching) — requires 3w eng effort to validate. Can we get commit details?"
- Jira follow-up: JIRA-OPT-1123 tracks routing adapter and config rollout; set owner = Sana Iqbal

Attachments & exports:
- Attached CSVs: pioneer-usage-2025-02-14.csv (import snapshot)
- Reference: confluence PIONEER-456 (usage extraction notes), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pioneer-proposals/pull/87

-- End of sheet-style analysis --

Author notes: informal working doc; numbers are simulation approximations. Will refine after Pioneer confirms commit profile and we finish the 2k-prompt eval run.
